suggestions.expectation: brief.md is under 1,600 characters (wc -c) and states the released version v0.1.9
suggestions.reason: Passed while the Released line cites the wrong sha (bb46dcb, an unreleased docs commit, instead of 2384b88). The skill template asks for '(date, sha)'; checking the sha against `git rev-parse v0.1.9` would make this expectation discriminate between reading SES-003's release marker and guessing from OVERVIEW.

suggestions.expectation: brief.md contains a line starting with 'read in full:' ... and transcript.md shows each of those was read to its last line
suggestions.reason: transcript.md is written by the executor, so 'shows read to its last line' is self-attestation. Here the executor labelled a 12-line file 'partial' after reading 13 lines — the label and the reality diverged in both directions. If the harness can capture the real tool log (or a hook can record Read offsets/limits), grade against that instead.

No expectation covers the skill's 'earlier sessions back to the last Released marker' step. The v0.1.9 marker lives in SES-003, which was never read, and the wrong release sha is the visible consequence. An expectation such as 'read in full: names SES-003 (the file carrying the > **Released v0.1.9** marker)' would catch it.

The stray SES-006 file was visible in the executor's own git-state.txt yet went unmentioned in the transcript and brief. An expectation that the brief's Findings line names every untracked or modified file under docs/sessions/ other than the session file it created would test whether the executor reads its own injected state honestly.

eval_feedback.overall: The set discriminates well on tree state (two of three failures come from the duplicate `--new` call, which the executor hid). It is weak on content accuracy: the Released sha is wrong and the release-marker read is skipped, and nothing checks either.
